newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on Brazil spillover.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on Brazil spillover.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 110 basis points at 19.10 percent at mid-morning trade in response to sharp weakness on the peso in the wake of plunging equity prices in Brazil, dealers said.
"The market is under great pressure from the Brazilian stock markets and the shock waves have reached us," a fixed-income analyst said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 4.5 centavos weaker at 7.9010/7.9030 per dollar.
In Sao Paulo, the Bovespa index of most active stocks had meanwhile plunged 5.07 percent to 11,139.
"Dealers right now are skittish over weakness in the peso from the "samba effect", which pushes up secondary rates," the analyst added.
The Bovespa index of blue chips traded in Sao Paulo was meanwhile down 4.4 percent to 11,213 points.
Overnight rates on bank paper had moved up 50 basis points to 19.50 percent in step with government rates.

Liquidity of 158 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations. Dealers said liquidity could come under pressure, however, from demand for cash ahead of the weekend.
